description: Mixed as-of primary-source extracts with cross-theme decoys. Inclusion is not an evaluator label.

documents.title: NYCB fourth-quarter 2023 results and capital actions
documents.body: NYCB recorded a $552 million provision for credit losses versus $62 million in Q3 and $185 million of net charge-offs, driven by two loans. Non-performing assets were 0.38% of assets; the allowance was $992 million and 232% of non-performing loans. The common dividend was cut to $0.05 as the bank accelerated capital building after crossing $100 billion in assets.

documents.title: Financial Stability Report near-term risks
documents.body: Market contacts viewed commercial real estate as a potential stress trigger because of rates, lower property values, and structural office-demand changes. Small and regional banks were viewed as more vulnerable because of higher commercial real-estate concentration.

documents.title: Third-quarter 2023 banking profile
documents.body: Noncurrent non-owner-occupied commercial-real-estate loans rose 36.4% sequentially and the noncurrent rate was the highest since Q3 2014. Industry unrealized securities losses were $683.9 billion, while deposit outflows were moderating.

documents.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
documents.title: Fall 2023 supervisory risk perspective
documents.body: The OCC said credit risk was increasing due partly to higher rates and commercial real estate, while the overall federal banking system remained sound.

documents.body: Unadjusted contemporaneous USD closes: NYCB 4.90, KRE 46.849998474121094, WAL 57.810001373291016. NYCB later completed a reverse split; 4.90 uses the contemporaneous pre-split price convention.

documents.title: Red Sea, Black Sea and Panama Canal trade disruptions
documents.body: Weekly container-ship transits had fallen 67% and major carriers had suspended Suez transits. Average Shanghai container spot rates had risen 122% since early December; Shanghai-Europe rates were up 256%. Longer routes increase fuel, insurance, labor, and vessel-capacity requirements.

documents.title: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden operational update
documents.body: Maersk said security risk remained significantly high, cancelled some bookings, and expected delays and significant network disruption.

documents.title: Suez Canal situation frequently asked questions
documents.body: Hapag-Lloyd continued Cape of Good Hope diversions until further notice because the Red Sea remained unsafe.

documents.title: January 2024 regional economic update
documents.body: As of January 21, ten-day cumulative Suez shipping volume was almost 50% below the prior year. Europe and Mediterranean to China freight costs had risen more than 400% since mid-November, reflecting insurance and longer-route costs.

documents.title: Eli Lilly first-quarter 2024 results
documents.body: Q1 2024 revenue rose 26%; new-product revenue increased by $1.79 billion to $2.39 billion, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound. Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance by $2 billion while still describing supply constraints and a manufacturing expansion plan.

documents.title: Novo Nordisk first-quarter 2024 results
documents.body: Novo Nordisk announced results for the first three months of 2024 and showed continued obesity-care growth. Its investor material described a gradual increase in Wegovy supply rather than unconstrained availability.

documents.title: Agreement to acquire three Catalent fill-finish sites
documents.body: Novo Nordisk agreed to acquire three fill-finish sites from Novo Holdings after Novo Holdings' planned Catalent acquisition. Closing depended on the Catalent transaction and approvals; additional filling capacity was expected gradually from 2026 onward.

documents.title: Novo Holdings agreement to acquire Catalent
documents.body: Novo Holdings agreed to acquire Catalent for $63.50 per share; three fill-finish sites were intended for sale to Novo Nordisk. The announced price represented a 16.5% premium to Catalent's February 2 close and 47.5% to its 60-day VWAP.

documents.title: Electricity 2024 executive summary
documents.body: The IEA estimated data-center, AI, and crypto electricity consumption could more than double from 460 TWh in 2022 to over 1,000 TWh in 2026.

documents.title: Twenty-year Microsoft PPA supports Crane restart
documents.body: Constellation announced a 20-year Microsoft PPA supporting restart of the 835 MW Crane Clean Energy Center. The restart targeted 2028 and required NRC approval plus state and local permits; Constellation expected about $1.6 billion of restart investment.

documents.title: Order on Susquehanna co-located load agreement
documents.body: FERC rejected without prejudice an amended PJM interconnection agreement increasing co-located load from 300 MW to 480 MW. The proceeding addressed tariff, reliability, cost-allocation, and service-obligation questions for co-located load.

documents.title: More than 70 MW of data-center infrastructure for Core42
documents.body: TeraWulf announced long-term leases to deliver more than 70 MW of data-center infrastructure for Core42 and G42 operations.
